## ✨ New Features

### Add controls to pause inbound operations while staging local changes ([#28625](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28625))

The beta stage controls expose `pauseInbound()` and `resumeInbound()` to control inbound operation processing without leaving staging mode. Await `pauseInbound()` before relying on inbound processing having stopped. Repeated pause or resume calls are idempotent.

Committing or discarding staged changes automatically releases any pause acquired through these controls, even if exiting staging mode throws. Pauses acquired by other code are preserved, and inbound signals are not paused.

While paused, the client's reference sequence number does not advance, which holds back the minimum sequence number for all clients. If the container reconnects while paused, it might not finish connecting until inbound processing resumes. Keep pauses short.

`pauseInbound` and `resumeInbound` are `undefined` if the container runtime does not support them, for example because it is an older version. Check that they are defined before calling them.

```typescript
const controls = containerRuntime.enterStagingMode();
if (controls.pauseInbound !== undefined) {
  await controls.pauseInbound();
}
// ... make staged changes ...
controls.commitChanges(); // Or controls.discardChanges().
```

Use `controls.resumeInbound?.()` to resume inbound operation processing while remaining in staging mode.

## 🌳 SharedTree DDS Changes

### Array move events now behave consistently before and after hydration ([#28487](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28487))

Range moves on unhydrated arrays now produce change events and deltas consistent with hydrated arrays, including when the destination is within the source range and the contents remain unchanged. This also makes insertion anchors update consistently before and after hydration.

Moving an empty range on unhydrated arrays no longer emits change events, matching hydrated arrays.

### Manage branch state independently of views ([#28520](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28520))

You can now create and retain an independent branch without keeping a typed view alive. This lets you separate the lifetime of branch state and history from the schema-configured view used to read and edit it.

This change is a step toward separating branch management from views and reducing the current one-view-per-branch restriction. It does not enable multiple active views of the same branch: each branch still supports one active view at a time.

Use the new alpha method `tree.forkBranch()` to create a `TreeBranchHandleAlpha` without a source view or schema configuration. Use `branch.viewWith(config)` when you need to read or edit the branch. Disposing that view preserves the branch so you can create another view later. Edits remain isolated until you merge them into another view.

```typescript
import {
  asAlpha,
  SchemaFactory,
  TreeViewConfiguration,
} from "@fluidframework/tree/alpha";

const sf = new SchemaFactory("counter");
class Counter extends sf.object("Counter", {
  count: sf.number,
}) {}

const config = new TreeViewConfiguration({ schema: Counter });

// `tree` is an `ITree` initialized with this schema and { count: 0 }.
// It has no active view.
const branch = asAlpha(tree).forkBranch();
const branchView = branch.viewWith(config);
const view = asAlpha(tree.viewWith(config));

branchView.root.count = 5;
console.log(view.root.count); // 0: the branch edit is isolated.

view.merge(branchView); // Also disposes branch and branchView.
console.log(view.root.count); // 5
```

You own each branch and must dispose it when you no longer need it. Disposing a branch also disposes its active view.

Use `branch.fork()` to create an independent child branch. Existing `view.fork()` behavior is unchanged: the returned view owns its branch, and disposing that view also disposes its branch.

See [Indexes and Branches](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/blob/main/packages/dds/tree/docs/main/indexes-and-branches.md) for more details.

### Reduce optimized forest memory overhead after loading and receiving inserted content ([#28653](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28653))

SharedTree configured with [ForestTypeOptimized](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/v3/tree#foresttypeoptimized-variable) now uses compact in-memory storage for eligible content loaded from summaries or received in insertion operations.

#### Example measurements

In a local benchmark with 10,000-character documents, the median results before and after this change were:

| Metric | Formatted text, before to after | Plain text, before to after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained tree heap after loading | 39.9 MiB to 30.6 MiB (23% less) | 5.12 MiB to 2.79 MiB (46% less) |
| Retained attached-content heap after loading | 19.8 MiB to 10.5 MiB (47% less) | 2.44 MiB to 0.113 MiB (95% less) |
| Summary load time | 140 ms to 212 ms (51% slower) | 28.5 ms to 40.2 ms (41% slower) |
| Receive insertion time | 271 ms to 428 ms (58% slower) | 242 ms to 63.0 ms (74% faster) |
| Local insertion time | 1,109 ms to 1,224 ms (10% slower) | 137 ms to 130 ms (5% faster) |

These measurements use Node.js 22, in-memory storage, and a mocked runtime, with 18 timed samples per case across two process orders. Heap measurements use six batches of loaded documents after garbage collection and do not measure peak memory. The memory savings can come with additional processing time, particularly when loading summaries or receiving formatted text. Results depend on the document schema, workload, and environment.

## ⚠️ Deprecations

### Deprecate isEquivalent compatibility flag ([#28655](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28655))

[`SchemaCompatibilityStatus.isEquivalent`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemacompatibilitystatus-interface#isequivalent-propertysignature) is deprecated. Use [`canView`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemacompatibilitystatus-interface#canview-propertysignature) to determine whether you can read and edit a document with your view schema. Use [`canUpgrade`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemacompatibilitystatus-interface#canupgrade-propertysignature) to determine whether you can upgrade the document's stored schema. For details about differences that prevent viewing, use [`SchemaCompatibilityStatusBeta.discrepancies`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemacompatibilitystatusbeta-interface#discrepancies-propertysignature).

There is no direct replacement for schema equivalence. The property remains available until a future major release.
